_comment: A blueprint never names a tool. It declares the CAPABILITY it needs (for example
'measure per-wakeup runqueue delay'). This file says which concrete tools can provide
that capability in a given environment, and the runtime binds one at execution time.
That separation is the point: swap babeltrace2 for Trace Compass, or for a vendor's own
in-house analyser, and the blueprint does not change. It is also what keeps the
architecture tool-agnostic and model-agnostic rather than being one more telemetry
Mahsa's finding still holds: what finally reaches the agent is an EXACT callable, not a
description. The difference is that the exact callable is produced by binding, not
hard-coded into the portable knowledge object.

Provider entries carry the metadata the binder needs to choose between alternatives: estimated overhead, platform, fidelity, permissions and tier. Escalation policy is cheapest-adequate-first: use evidence that already exists, then low-overhead active collection, and only escalate to high-fidelity tracing when the cheaper tier leaves the question open.

Every binding resolves through $BLUEPRINT_HOME, the root of a blueprints checkout. Nothing here names an absolute path, so the same blueprint runs from a checkout on a laptop, on a cluster, or on a partner's host without editing.

kernel.scheduler.runqueue_delay.what: For each wakeup, the delay between a thread becoming runnable and a CPU actually running it. Reported per process, baseline window vs incident window.

providers.available_when: babeltrace2 >= 2.1 on PATH and a CTF trace directory
providers.notes: Our traces carry CTF 2 metadata (JSON preamble). babeltrace 2.0.x rejects it; use the 2.1 wrapper so its lib directory precedes the system one.
requires_permissions: root or CAP_SYS_ADMIN for kernel tracing
providers.produces_contract: per-process p50/p95/p99 runqueue delay, baseline vs incident

providers.available_when: Trace Compass with the kernel analysis module
providers.notes: Trace Compass exposes the same scheduler analysis through its Critical Path / CPU usage views. Left unbound deliberately: it is Sneh's area, and the point of this registry is that binding it later requires no blueprint change.

providers.available_when: a BPF runqueue-latency collector is installed
providers.notes: Cheaper than full kernel tracing and sufficient to detect contention, but it gives a histogram rather than per-event data, so it cannot be re-attributed to services afterwards. The binder should prefer this tier first and escalate to the tracer only if attribution is actually needed.

kernel.syscall.blocking_duration.what: How long a process stays inside each syscall between entry and exit, per (process, syscall), baseline vs incident.

providers.available_when: babeltrace2 >= 2.1 on PATH and a CTF trace directory
requires_permissions: root or CAP_SYS_ADMIN for kernel tracing
providers.produces_contract: per (process, syscall) duration percentiles, baseline vs incident
providers.notes: Syscall entry+exit is the most expensive collection in these blueprints, because every syscall generates two events. Scope it to the suspect processes.

traces.call_graph.convergence.what: Caller-to-callee edge latency change, and which component the slow edges converge on without having slow outgoing edges of its own.
requires_events: distributed trace spans with parent links

providers.available_when: the run carries OTLP spans
providers.produces_contract: ranked convergence candidates with incoming/outgoing slowdown
providers.notes: Reads spans that were already collected, so it costs nothing extra. This is why it runs first in both blueprints. Takes the trace directory only; it must not need an application name, which an operator working a live incident does not have.

metrics.container.cpu_attribution.what: CPU consumed per container, baseline vs incident, cross-referenced against which containers appear in the call graph.

providers.available_when: the run carries container metrics
providers.notes: Takes the trace directory only; it must not need an application name, which an operator working a live incident does not have.

verdict.dependency_wait.what: Combine convergence, blocking duration and the runqueue control into a single verdict, including a refusal plus redirect when the evidence points elsewhere.

providers.available_when: always

trace.stage_ctf.what: Make stored kernel traces readable by a CTF reader, wherever they are held.

providers.available_when: <trace_dir> already contains an uncompressed CTF directory
providers.notes: The common case in a live deployment: the collector wrote CTF and nothing needs staging.

providers.available_when: <trace_dir> holds a gzipped CTF archive
providers.notes: Expands about sevenfold. Our own archive is stored this way.

kernel.scheduler.oncpu_attribution.what: On-CPU time per process, baseline window vs incident window, derived from the per-CPU gaps between context switches. Yields host utilisation, the cores each process gained or lost, and whether any process is new to the CPU.

providers.available_when: babeltrace2 >= 2.1 on PATH and a CTF trace directory
providers.notes: One tracepoint is enough. Validated by recovering the injected cgroup cap of the noisy-neighbour recipe to within 1% (1.0 -> measured 0.988-0.997; 2.0 -> measured 1.978-2.002).
requires_permissions: root or CAP_SYS_ADMIN for kernel tracing
providers.produces_contract: per-process cores baseline vs incident, host utilisation per window, newcomer and loser lists

providers.available_when: container metrics are already being scraped
providers.notes: Container CPU counters answer the same question more cheaply when they already exist, but attribute per container rather than per process and miss anything outside a container.

network.retransmission_rate.what: Share of TCP segments that repeat a sequence number already seen on the same flow, per interface, baseline window vs incident window. A repeat means the original was lost and re-sent.

providers.available_when: babeltrace2 >= 2.1 on PATH and a CTF trace directory
providers.notes: Two traps, both measured. The same packet fires the event on more than one interface (veth then bridge), so buffers must be de-duplicated by skbaddr or every run reports about 50%. And the interface field must not be matched inside `procname`.
requires_permissions: root or CAP_SYS_ADMIN for kernel tracing
providers.produces_contract: per-interface retransmission and drop rates, both windows, plus the list of impaired interfaces

network.queue_drop_rate.what: Share of buffers queued to a device that are never transmitted - dropped inside the queueing discipline. Per interface, both windows.

providers.available_when: babeltrace2 >= 2.1 on PATH and a CTF trace directory
providers.notes: Both events carry skbaddr, so a queued buffer with no matching transmit was dropped. Rates are small (0.06-0.29% on impaired runs) because the trace samples the loss, so this corroborates rather than decides.
requires_permissions: root or CAP_SYS_ADMIN for kernel tracing
providers.produces_contract: per-interface retransmission and drop rates, both windows, plus the list of impaired interfaces

storage.io_attribution.what: Disk requests per second attributed to the issuing process, plus service time per device, baseline window vs incident window.

providers.available_when: babeltrace2 >= 2.1 on PATH and a CTF trace directory
providers.notes: block_rq_issue names the issuing process directly, so the culprit comes free. Requests are matched to completions by device and sector. Service time is produced but must NOT be used to decide - measured to stay flat or fall under disk flooding.
requires_permissions: root or CAP_SYS_ADMIN for kernel tracing
providers.produces_contract: per-process request rate both windows, per-device service time, queue depth, and the I/O newcomer if one exists

process.creation_attribution.what: Process creation per second attributed to the child command name, baseline window vs incident window, and the command whose rate rose most.

providers.available_when: babeltrace2 >= 2.1 on PATH and a CTF trace directory
providers.notes: The host total is not decisive: measured at 134 forks/s baseline on an idle Sock Shop, so a fork storm only lifts it 1.77x. The arriving process moves 27x. This capability therefore contracts to deliver the newcomer, not the sum.
requires_permissions: root or CAP_SYS_ADMIN for kernel tracing
providers.produces_contract: per-window rates plus the newcomer: the key whose rate rose most, what it was before, and what it is now

network.egress_attribution.what: Outbound bytes per second attributed to the sending process, baseline window vs incident window, and the process whose rate rose most.

providers.available_when: babeltrace2 >= 2.1 on PATH and a CTF trace directory
providers.notes: The host total is application-specific - the same absolute transfer is 6.2x on one application and 24.9x on the other - so a ratio over the host cannot transfer. The per-process gain is 8.1e7 bytes/s on both.
requires_permissions: root or CAP_SYS_ADMIN for kernel tracing
providers.produces_contract: per-window rates plus the newcomer: the key whose rate rose most, what it was before, and what it is now

syscall.error_attribution.what: Failing syscalls per second by errno and by call name, both windows, from the return value on syscall exit.

providers.available_when: babeltrace2 >= 2.1 on PATH and a CTF trace directory
providers.notes: The total failing-syscall rate is useless: the baseline already runs ~16,000 per second, almost all EAGAIN on non-blocking reads. Only the per-errno rate carries a fault.
requires_permissions: root or CAP_SYS_ADMIN for kernel tracing
providers.produces_contract: per-window rates plus the newcomer: the key whose rate rose most, what it was before, and what it is now

verdict.apply_rules.what: Apply the blueprint decision rules to a finished evidence pack and return a verdict with every gate it tested, so the reasoning is inspectable rather than a bare answer.

providers.available_when: python3 and an evidence pack produced by the earlier steps

report.decision_card.what: Draw one page showing why the decision was reached: the deciding signal against every fault family known to the library, resources and waiting before and during, every gate with its margin, and what was ruled out.

providers.available_when: python3 and a reference distribution at $BLUEPRINT_HOME/results/ruler.json
providers.notes: The SVG carries a plain-text <desc> with every number on the page, so an agent can read the findings without rendering anything.

report.recommended_action.what: Turn a verdict into an explanation and a recommended action, both in plain language, for a human who has to act on it.

providers.available_when: python3 and a verdict from verdict.apply_rules

kernel.interrupt.time_attribution.what: Time spent handling device interrupts and in futex waits, baseline window against incident window.

providers.available_when: babeltrace2 >= 2.1 on PATH and a CTF trace directory
providers.notes: Interrupt time separates a container at its memory limit from a disk flood, but only in combination with disk arrivals - neither works alone.

escalation_policy.rule: Never start at the most expensive tier. Escalate only when the evidence sufficiency check leaves a candidate cause unresolved, and record why.
escalation_policy.source: architecture note: use existing telemetry before enabling additional tracing; request deeper telemetry only when basic evidence is inconclusive
